modificaciones_necesarias: [Apollo 13]: 1) Add a third O2 tank isolated in another compartment; 2) Upgrade thermostats to withstand 65 V DC; 3) Remove mechanical stirring fans inside O2 tanks; 4) Encase wiring in stainless-steel sheathing; 5) Reform detanking test procedures and manufacturing change control.

[Apollo 1]: 1) Redesign a unified quick-opening hatch (opens outward in 3 s from inside or outside); 2) Replace the 100% O2 launch atmosphere with a 60% O2 / 40% N2 mix on the pad; 3) Strictly restrict and relocate combustible materials (Velcro, nylon) and adopt Beta cloth fabrics / fire-resistant suits; 4) Shield wiring and plumbing to the Block II standard; 5) Mandatory hazardous-test protocols with on-site rescue.

[PSI-181: Pb-Sn and Sn-Ag-Cu solders in microgravity and extreme temperatures (ISSI)]: 1) Use solder wire without a volatile flux core, or apply vacuum/ultrasonic degassing during in-orbit electronic repairs (in-space manufacturing/repair), to avoid trapped pores that create hot spots and electrical ignition; 2) Prefer doped SAC formulations with intermetallic control for lunar missions with cryogenic cycling.

[ISSI Lunar/Mars (PSI-181): soldering, electronic repair and the cryogenic lunar night]: 1) Require vacuum-assisted reflow or fluxless ultrasonic soldering for all electronic repairs on the Moon and Mars; 2) Derate by 25% the maximum current of traces and solder joints operating in 34% O2 exploration atmospheres.
[Li-ion batteries (NESC / Gateway HALO)]: Enforce strict state-of-charge limits in transit, FTRC thermal isolation between cells, HALO containment bags and dedicated ECLSS catalysts for HF/POF3.
[Apollo LM 100% O2 (5 psia) — Beta Cloth & Velcro]: Use Beta Cloth as a fire barrier in MLI blankets and strictly restrict any Velcro-type fastener in enriched atmospheres.
[xEMU / AxEMU suits (4.3 psia, 100% O2) + lunar dust]: Hermetic isolation of O2 paths, NASA-STD-6001 Test 13/14 testing and electrostatic cleaning protocols before depressurization.

[Lunar Gateway HALO / Orion OLIF / GIEM model]: Integrate GIEM autonomous software for instant IMV shut-off, portable extinguishing compatible with 0 g/0.16 g, and activated-carbon beds + TCCS catalytic oxidation.
[Mars Ascent Vehicle (MAV) NTO/MMH & MON-25 hypergolics]: Use double isolation on helium lines, strict pre/post-firing purging and external decontamination protocols before entering the habitat.

modificaciones_necesarias: [FLEX]: 1) Raise the minimum concentrations of inert suppressant gases (N2, CO2, He) above terrestrial standards; 2) Add infrared/spectral sensors to detect invisible cool flames and keep post-extinction monitoring to prevent spontaneous reignition.
[FLEX-2]: 1) Update engine and thruster kinetic models with slow radiative and convective droplet-droplet coupling; 2) Adjust injection spacing in droplet arrays to mitigate soot and reignition.

[Cool Flames (iniciativa)]: 1) Update post-fire procedures on the ISS/Artemis to require full cooling and controlled venting of partially oxidized vapours (formaldehyde/CO) before reopening compartments where a flame seemed to go out.
[Cool flames]: Add mid-wave IR cameras and CO/formaldehyde sensors to verify complete chemical (not just visual) extinction after a fire.

[PSI-68: FLEX-2 (Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2)]: 1) Integrate low-temperature kinetic sub-mechanisms (NTC / RO2 alkyl peroxides) into space propulsion and safety CFD models to predict cool flames (550-750 K); 2) Install UV (OH* at 310 nm) + UV/visible (HCHO* at 395 nm) and IR optical diagnostics in combustion chambers and habitats; 3) Raise the CO2/N2 dilution margin by at least +4% to suppress both the hot-flame and cool-flame branches in heavy hydrocarbons.

[PSI-69: FLEX (Flame Extinguishment Experiment)]: 1) Raise the design concentration of inert agents (N2, CO2) by +3 to +5% relative to terrestrial NFPA standards; 2) Add spectral monitoring of excited formaldehyde (HCHO*) and mid-infrared after any apparent extinction of liquid hydrocarbons.

[PSI-39: CFI (Cool Flames Investigation)]: 1) Differentiate in-orbit safety and suppression protocols by the liquid's molecular structure (linear alkanes with a high risk of invisible cool flames vs esters/alcohols without an NTC branch).

[PSI-108: STDCE-1 (Surface Tension Driven Convection Experiment - 1)]: 1) Include Marangoni thermocapillary shear-stress boundary conditions (d_sigma/dT) in flame-spread models over liquids and molten polymer pools in microgravity.

[PSI-117: Multiphysics CFD dynamics of cool flames under thermoconvective perturbation]: 1) Avoid sudden ventilation pulses over post-extinction hydrocarbon vapour clouds, since the convective wake concentrates RO2/H2O2 radicals and triggers secondary hot reignition.

[PSI-142: Cool-flame transitions in radiative and strain extinction]: 1) Update strain-extinction criteria (critical Damköhler number) in space engines and suppression systems using the 4-branch S-curve that includes the cool-flame regime.

[PSI-159: ACME / CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases)]: 1) Extend cool-flame detection protocols (HCHO* and CO sensors) to leaks of light gaseous hydrocarbons (propane, butane, pentane) in space thermal and propulsion systems.

[FLEX & CFI partial-g: cool flames and fuel droplets on the Moon and Mars]: 1) In lunar/Martian solvent stores, laboratories and greenhouses, keep forced extraction >25 cm/s or inert with CO2/N2 after any liquid incident to prevent reignition by a cool-flame buoyant plume.

[PSI-21: ACME / CLD Flame (Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame)]: 1) Recalibrate the edge/triple-flame stabilization and soot-radiation sub-models in CFD codes for low-emission combustors and space burners.

[PSI-22: ACME / E-FIELD Flames (Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames)]: 1) Add high-voltage electrode rings/meshes (6-9 kV, < 1 W) to orbital burners and incinerators to replace mechanical fans with ionic-wind convection and eliminate soot emission.

[PSI-23: ACME / s-Flame (Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames)]: 1) Include pulsating diffusive-thermal instability criteria (Le > 1) and CO2/H2O radiative reabsorption in spherical fire spread and extinction models for space cabins.

[PSI-60: Computational and experimental analysis of SPICE data]: 1) Couple optically thin/thick radiation models with OH- and O2-radical soot oxidation kinetics to predict sudden soot release (wing/tip opening) in space fires.

[PSI-106: SLICE (Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment)]: 1) Design flame holders in space combustion systems taking into account that liftoff height in 0 g is more sensitive to the coflow momentum deficit.

[PSI-107: SPICE (Smoke Point In Coflow Experiment)]: 1) Apply a 3x safety reduction factor to terrestrial smoke-point tables (ASTM D1322) when assessing soot propensity and HEPA filter loading in space fires.

[ACME E-FIELD Lunar/Mars: emulating partial gravity with ionic wind]: 1) Use the PSI-22 (E-FIELD) voltage-gravity correlation to qualify burners, regolith-processing torches and methane leak sensors (CH4/LOX) for lunar and Martian missions.
[MRE (Molten Regolith Electrolysis) — LR-1 / ASSIST]: Run MRE reactors in isolated vacuum zones, away from pressurized habitats, with infrared thermal monitoring and fast shut-off valves.
[CaRD (COPR), hydrogen ilmenite reduction and np-Fe0 microwaves]: Implement continuous N2 purging in closed CaRD/ilmenite loops, H2/CO detection and microwave power control with thermal feedback.

[MOXIE (Perseverance) + 200x scale-up to 24 t LOX/CH4 Sabatier]: Site the MOXIE/Sabatier plant at a safe distance from the crew habitat, with remote leak sensors, fast shut-off valves and safe venting.
[Metal/CO2 combustion (magnesium/aluminum) & SAM Curiosity]: Do not assume Martian atmospheric CO2 makes all reactive metal powders inert; isolate Mg/Al powders in sealed storage.

modificaciones_necesarias: [BRE]: 1) Calibrate the feedback between surface thermocouples, radiant heat-flux sensors and the gas mass-flow valve to emulate the mass-transfer B-number of real polymers in space habitats.

[BASS]: 1) Revise NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (upward burning in 1 g) because it underestimates flammability in microgravity at low flows (~1-10 cm/s); 2) Prohibit applying slow localized N2 jets directly at the flame base without first cutting HVAC ventilation, since entrained O2 intensifies the fire.
[Flammability limit]: Lower the maximum allowed oxygen threshold (MOC) in space-material certification tables by an extra 2-4% O2 relative to 1 g ground tests.
[NASA standard test]: Replace or complement NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 with slow opposed-flow tests and a Narrow Channel apparatus calibrated with BASS and SoFIE data.
[Spread direction]: Reverse the geometry of firebreak barriers and the placement of thermal sensors in ducts/racks so they also watch upstream (toward the ventilation air inlet).
[Spacecraft ventilation]: Automate an immediate HVAC ventilation shutoff (flow to 0 cm/s) on detecting smoke or flame radiation, before discharging the extinguishing agent.
[Localized suppression]: Redesign extinguisher nozzles with total-flooding diffusers or enveloping mist instead of narrow inert-gas jets that induce O2 mixing.

[PSI-25: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids - II)]: 1) Lower the MOC certification threshold for cabin polymers and textiles to <= 15.0% O2 for slow-ventilation regimes (0.5-8 cm/s); 2) Add two-branch extinction curves (radiative quenching < 1 cm/s and convective blowoff > 30 cm/s) to the Orion/Gateway fire code; 3) Require a waiting time after ventilation shutoff (> 60 s) because of the thermal inertia of thick solids (PMMA >= 3.2 mm).

[PSI-26: BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids)]: 1) Prohibit narrow N2-jet extinguisher nozzles without first cutting ventilation; 2) Reorient thermal sensors upstream of electronic components; 3) Replace the one-dimensional criterion of NASA-STD-6001 Test 1.

[PSI-62: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling (FGM & Two-Color Tomography)]: 1) Adopt pre-integrated Unsteady Flamelet Generated Manifold (UFGM) tables with non-adiabatic radiative losses in cabin-certification CFD codes; 2) Calibrate soot-emission models with volume-fraction profiles measured by two-color optical tomography.

[PSI-20: ACME / BRE (Burning Rate Emulator)]: 1) Use the BRE parameter matrix (heat of gasification L_g and B-number) to pre-screen candidate cabin polymers without burning hundreds of solid samples in orbit.

[LUCI & FM2: flammability at lunar gravity (0.16 g) and the U-shaped LOI curve]: 1) Replace terrestrial NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (1 g) certification with tests or correction factors at the minimum of the U-shaped LOI curve (equivalent flow of 6.5-8.0 cm/s for lunar 0.16 g); 2) Build into the prediction engine the intrinsic buoyant velocity V_eff = sqrt(V_forced^2 + V_buoyant(g)^2) and de Ris scaling (V_f ~ (k*rho*c)^(-1) for thin solids).

modificaciones_necesarias: [SoFIE]: 1) Certify all cabin polymers (PMMA, Delrin, fabrics) under low-pressure, high-O2 exploration atmospheres (up to 40% O2 and 0.2-1.5 atm) with real HVAC ventilation flows (0-30 cm/s).

[SoFIE: Flammability correlation]: 1) Replace the single pass/fail criterion of NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 with multidimensional maps of the maximum oxygen concentration (MOC) as a function of forced-flow velocity and pressure.
[SoFIE: Growth and extinction]: 1) Include the solid's internal preheating and surface curvature in predictive radiative-extinction models.
[SoFIE: Thermal and species fields]: 1) Set minimum safe thicknesses for cabin coatings and plastic films below the thermal/species spread threshold.

[SoFIE: External heat flux]: 1) Cut the maximum allowed radiant heat flux near electronics and cables in spacecraft by 50% relative to the terrestrial standard; 2) Increase thermal insulation in power racks.

[SoFIE: Narrow Channel]: 1) Adopt the Narrow Channel Apparatus in ground laboratories as a standard complementary method to, or replacement for, NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 to pre-certify space materials in 1 g.
[Ignition]: Halve the maximum allowed temperature/heat flux on surfaces near cables and batteries; reinforce fast-acting circuit breakers.

[PSI-98: SAFFIRE-I (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - I)]: 1) Update cabin emergency-response models with the large-scale steady spread rate and the fast pressure/temperature rise in a closed volume; 2) Validate that cutting ventilation immediately stops a 0.4 m-wide flame front.

[PSI-99: SAFFIRE-II (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - II)]: 1) Penalize in certification protocols geometries with exposed edges, grooves or ribs in thick polymers (PMMA/polycarbonate), since they sustain the flame when the flat surface does not burn; 2) Restrict silicone membranes thinner than 1.5 mm in ducts with flow >= 20 cm/s.

[PSI-100: SAFFIRE-III (Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment - III)]: 1) Limit the maximum air velocity in space-habitat corridors and plenums to < 15 cm/s; 2) Size post-fire pressure relief and CO/CO2 scrubbing systems for heat release rates that scale linearly with ventilation velocity.

[SAFFIRE IV-VI & SoFIE SEA: Lunar/Martian atmospheres (8.2 psia / 34% O2)]: 1) Prohibit materials certified only at 21% O2 inside modules pressurized to 8.2 psia / 34% O2 (HLS, Gateway, lunar/Martian rovers); 2) Install far-field catalytic scrubbers (Far-Field Scrubbers for CO, CO2, HCl and HF tested in SAFFIRE IV-VI) and a rapid post-fire depressurization/repressurization protocol.

[MARS-0.38g & CO2-ISRU: combustion at Martian gravity and CO2 diluent]: 1) Use purified, compressed Martian atmospheric CO2 as the primary flooding and inerting fire system in Martian habitats; 2) Physically isolate solid-oxide electrolysis ISRU plants (MOXIE type, 800 °C, high-purity O2) outside the pressurized habitable volume.
[SoFIE (ISS CIR - GEL, MIST, SMuRF, RTDFS, NCA)]: Make the 5 SoFIE sub-projects a mandatory calibration reference for SEA atmospheres (34-37% O2) and radiative safety factors.
[LUCI (Lunar-g Combustion Investigation)]: Calibrate Artemis certification criteria (HLS/habitats) with LUCI 0.16 g data instead of interpolating linearly between 0 g and 1 g.
[FM2 (Flammability of Materials on the Moon)]: Establish FM2 as the final validation standard for Human Landing System (HLS) and lunar habitat interior materials.
[ZGF Drop Tower Centrifuge 0.16g]: Include Coriolis correction in centrifuge CFD simulations and use 6.8 cm/s as the lunar equivalent buoyant velocity.
[SEA 8.2 psia / 34-37% O2: Nomex vs 60% Kevlar / 40% PBI]: Ban standard Nomex and nylon in critical SEA 34-37% O2 zones; require 60% Kevlar / 40% PBI in lunar restraint nets and softgoods.

[NASA-STD-6001B Test 4 (cables) & Tests 13/14/17 (O2 compatibility)]: Require a Test 4 pass at the SEA worst case (37% O2) with AFCI protection and ultra-strict cleaning of oxygen lines certified by Tests 13/14/17.
[Spread at Martian gravity 0.38 g (the 1 g vs 0.38 g vs 0 g gap)]: Apply the effective velocity V_eff = sqrt(V_forced^2 + V_b(0.38g)^2) in Mars habitat risk calculations.
[In-situ Martian N2/Ar atmosphere (34% O2, 41.3% N2, 24.6% Ar)]: Validate all Mars habitat materials directly in the 34% O2 / 41.3% N2 / 24.6% Ar mixture before certification.
[Martian inflatable habitats (8.2 psia) & Li-ion FTRC at 0.38 g]: Combine 60% Kevlar / 40% PBI inner barriers, AFCI breakers, SOC limits and FTRC thermal isolation between Li-ion cells.

modificaciones_necesarias: [SAME]: 1) Redesign the laser-scattering optical chambers and threshold algorithms of space smoke detectors (Orion/Gateway/Lunar Lander) to detect the larger particle distributions produced by slow pyrolysis in 0 g.
[DAFT]: 1) Add multi-wavelength discriminating filtering and lunar/ambient dust rejection to fire sensors to avoid false alarms from suspended dust after EVAs.
[Smoke detection]: Recalibrate optical scattering angles and detection algorithms for the large agglomerated particles typical of microgravity.

[PSI-101: SAME-R (Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight)]: 1) Replace ionization smoke detectors (designed for ultrafine particles < 0.1 microns in 1 g) with laser-scattering photoelectric detectors calibrated for the 0.3-1.5 micron range measured in SAME-R; 2) Include coagulation-compensation algorithms for slow transport through the cabin.

[PSI-102: SAME (Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment)]: 1) Deploy dual-wavelength (blue + near-infrared) smoke sensors that measure the size-moment ratio (mean diameter) at the same time, to tell Teflon/wire pyrolysis (small particles) from silicone/cellulose smoke or ambient dust.

[PSI-47: DAFT / DAFT-2 (Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test)]: 1) Exploit the low cabin background of ultrafine particles (thanks to HEPA filtering) by setting early pre-alarm thresholds on condensation-nucleus counts (CPC) for incipient electrical overloads; 2) Temporarily mask the pre-alarm in the food-warmer (galley) area.

[PSI-115: Advanced modelling of smoke generation (SAME data)]: 1) Integrate the aerosol population-balance module (PBM with fractal dimension 1.8) into habitat ventilation simulation software (Orion/Gateway) to optimize the placement of photoelectric detectors.

[SAME/DAFT Lunar & Mars dust: telling regolith dust from smoke]: 1) Require multi-criteria smoke detectors (two-wavelength laser scattering + optical depolarization + electrochemical CO cell) in all EVA airlocks and lunar/Martian cabins; 2) Enable a dust false-alarm suppression mode synchronized with airlock pressurization without disabling the CO/pyrolysis channel.
[NASA-STD-6001B & JSC 20584 SMAC / NASA-STD-3001]: Require T_grp < 1 verification after suppression, HEPA filtration <= 0.1 mg/m3 and HF/HCl acid-gas monitoring in Artemis and Mars habitats.
[Suitports vs lunar airlocks]: Prioritize suitports in pressurized rovers and lunar habitats; redundant thermal seals resistant to regolith abrasion.
[Electrostatic lunar dust (UV/triboelectric) and EDS shields]: Deploy Electrodynamic Dust Shields (EDS) on visors, radiators and seals, plus continuous grounding of suits and LTV rovers.
[Martian dust storms, Paschen minimum & SuperCam ESD]: Install Electrostatic Precipitators (ESP) and Electrodynamic Shields (EDS) on all ISRU atmospheric intakes and Martian airlocks.

[Martian perchlorates (ClO4-) & Mars Dust Working Group toxicology]: Implement biological/chemical/electrostatic ClO4- scrubbing, strict HEPA filtration (<=0.1 mg/m3) and GASP optical anti-false-alarm algorithms.

entries.experimento_investigacion: Apollo 13 (CSM-109 / LM-7)
entries.categoria: Spacecraft accident
entries.instalacion_hardware: Apollo CSM-109 Service Module (Oxygen Tank 2) / LM-7 Aquarius
entries.investigador_responsable: NASA SMA / Apollo 13 Review Board (Cortright Commission)
entries.fecha_periodo: 1970-04 (third day of the mission; splashdown 17 Apr 1970)
entries.material_combustible: Cryogenic oxygen; Teflon wiring insulation
entries.condiciones: Heaters on for ~8 h up to ~1000 °F (final pad test); 65 V DC
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Oxygen tank 2 exploded: heaters raised from 28 to 65 V DC without upgrading the thermostats; overheating during the pad test damaged the insulation
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Damage to tank 1, loss of fuel cells, power and water; lunar mission aborted; crew returned alive using the lunar module as a lifeboat
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Add a third O2 tank isolated in another compartment; 2) Upgrade thermostats to withstand 65 V DC; 3) Remove mechanical stirring fans inside O2 tanks; 4) Encase wiring in stainless-steel sheathing; 5) Reform detanking test procedures and manufacturing change control.
entries.fuente: NASA SMA - Apollo 13

entries.experimento_investigacion: Apollo 1 (AS-204, CM-012)
entries.categoria: Spacecraft accident
entries.instalacion_hardware: Apollo Command Module CM-012 (Launch Complex 34)
entries.investigador_responsable: NASA SMA / Apollo 204 Review Board
entries.material_combustible: Combustible materials inside the cabin (nylon, Velcro, foam); pure oxygen atmosphere
entries.condiciones: Cabin pressurized with 100% oxygen (16.7 psi), hatches closed, suits on; three-piece hatch that took ~90 s to open under ideal conditions
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Sudden fire in the command module during an internal-power test (Plugs-Out Test); evidence of electrical arcing in vulnerable wiring near the environmental control system
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Three astronauts died of CO and toxic-gas asphyxiation; pressure vessel ruptured; test wrongly classified as non-hazardous, with no rescue protocol
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Redesign a unified quick-opening hatch (opens outward in 3 s from inside or outside); 2) Replace the 100% O2 launch atmosphere with a 60% O2 / 40% N2 mix on the pad; 3) Strictly restrict and relocate combustible materials (Velcro, nylon) and adopt Beta cloth fabrics / fire-resistant suits; 4) Shield wiring and plumbing to the Block II standard; 5) Mandatory hazardous-test protocols with on-site rescue.
entries.fuente: NASA SMA - Apollo 1

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: MHD flow and nucleation in Zr64Ni36 (Cycles 9, 19, 22, 23, 26, 29)
entries.categoria: MHD / solidification and flow in liquid metals (ISS-EML)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Electromagnetic Levitator (EML) - Batch 2
entries.investigador_responsable: R. W. Hyers, G. P. Bracker (WPI / UMass), D. M. Matson, K. F. Kelton
entries.material_combustible: Molten metal alloy Zr64Ni36 (8.0 mm sphere, sigma = 7.271e5 S/m)
entries.condiciones: Electromagnetic levitation in microgravity; T = 1040-1760 K; heater current 17.5-55.7 A; positioner 140.8-191.7 A; 458 CFD files + 2 telemetry CSVs in part-01
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Characterize MHD flow velocity, Reynolds number and shear-strain rate during cooling to recalescence, to study cavitation/flow-induced dynamic nucleation
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: In Cycles 19, 22, 23 the flow is laminar (Re = 0.69-0.92, shear = 5.6-6.5 1/s); in Cycles 26 and 29, with the heater on, the flow is initially turbulent (Re > 600 above 1720 K and 1460 K) and crosses the laminar-turbulent transition; the cooling rate (0.02-1.33 °C/s) was an order of magnitude lower than in the SRD (10 °C/s)
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Switch from the laminar model to the RNG k-epsilon turbulent model above 1460 K (Cycle 29) and 1720 K (Cycle 26); 2) Recalculate the target shear-strain rate for the real slow cooling rates (0.02-1.33 °C/s) so that concentration profiles around subcritical nuclei do not interact; 3) Turn off the heater control voltage (0.000 V) during the free-cooling phase.
entries.fuente: Carpeta part-01: PSI-166_Reports_Updated ZrNi Report.pdf & 458 archivos Raw Data ZrNi

entries.material_combustible: Metallic-glass-forming alloy Cu50Zr50 (6.5 mm sphere, sigma = 7.05e5 S/m)

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-166: Quasicrystal nucleation in Ti39.5Zr39.5Ni21 (Cycles 11, 49, 50, 53, 55, 62, 64, 65, 66)

entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Electromagnetic Levitator (EML) - Batch 2.1
entries.investigador_responsable: R. W. Hyers, G. P. Bracker, K. F. Kelton (Washington U.)
entries.material_combustible: Quasicrystal-forming alloy Ti39.5Zr39.5Ni21 (6.0 mm sphere, liquidus 1093 K)
entries.condiciones: Undercooling of ~150 K (recalescence at 980-1032 K); positioner 3.87-9.39 V; 12 FluentMagData zip files and 3 reports in part-01
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Check whether the shear-strain rate meets the SRD requirement to avoid collisions between the diffusion fields of critical and subcritical nuclei

entries.material_combustible: Antimony (Sb)-doped germanium (10^19 /cm3, 8.0 mm sphere, sigma = 1.52e6 S/m)
entries.condiciones: T = 1158-1310 K; oscillating-drop method; 33 Raw Data Ge files and Final Ge Report.pdf in part-01
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Explain the 1 to 2 orders-of-magnitude discrepancy between the viscosity measured in ISS-EML (0.0029 Pa·s), parabolic flights (0.0124-0.0136 Pa·s) and a rotating cup on Earth (4.55e-4 Pa·s)

entries.codigo_corto: PSI-25: BASS-II (Burning and Suppression of Solids - II)
entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-25: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II) in the ISS MSG
entries.categoria: Sólidos / inflamabilidad y supresión en microgravedad (Repositorio NASA PSI-25)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / modified SPICE flow duct (7.6 x 7.6 cm section)
entries.investigador_responsable: S. L. Olson, P. V. Ferkul (NASA GRC), J. S. T'ien (CWRU), C. Fernandez-Pello (UC Berkeley), I. S. Wichman (MSU), F. J. Miller (SDSU)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS Expeditions 38-40 (2014) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-25
entries.material_combustible: Flat black and clear PMMA plates (1.2-6.35 mm), PMMA cylinders (6.35-12.7 mm), PMMA spheres (19 mm), SIBAL fabric (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass), thin cotton, Nomex and Ultem film
entries.condiciones: Opposed and concurrent forced flow from 0 to 53 cm/s (high sensitivity at 0.4-10 cm/s); N2 vitiation from 21.8% down to 13.5% O2 (MOC/LOI determination); cabin pressure ~100.5-101.5 kPa; radiometer, thermocouples and HD video

entries.experimento_investigacion: PSI-68: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2 (FLEX-2) in the ISS CIR / MDCA
entries.categoria: Combustión de gotas aisladas, mezclas bicomponente y llamas frías (Repositorio NASA PSI-68)
entries.instalacion_hardware: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) / Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
entries.investigador_responsable: F. A. Williams (UCSD), F. L. Dryer (Princeton), V. Nayagam (CWRU), D. L. Dietrich & M. C. Hicks (NASA GRC), T. I. Farouk (USC)
entries.fecha_periodo: ISS Expeditions 29-45 (2012-2015) / NASA PSI Public Archive PSI-68
entries.material_combustible: Free or SiC-fiber-supported liquid droplets (D0 = 1.8 to 5.0 mm): n-heptane, n-decane, n-octane, n-dodecane, methanol, ethanol, PRF blends (n-heptane/iso-octane), jet-fuel surrogates (decane/propylbenzene) and binary droplet arrays
entries.condiciones: Ambient pressure 0.5 to 3.0 atm (50.6 to 304.0 kPa); O2 concentration 12% to 40%; N2, CO2, He and Xe diluents; quiescent environment (0 cm/s) and slow convective flow by translation (0.5 to 22 cm/s); droplet spacing L/D0 = 2 to 12
entries.descripcion_objetivo: Quantify the burning-rate constant K (d^2 law: D^2 = D0^2 - K*t), soot-shell formation, radiative extinction of the hot flame, transition to two-stage combustion (cool flames at 550-750 K) and droplet-droplet interaction
entries.consecuencia_hallazgo: Large linear alkanes (n-heptane, n-decane, n-dodecane) undergo radiative extinction of the visible hot flame but keep vaporizing through invisible cool flames governed by NTC (negative temperature coefficient) chemistry, which can produce an explosive vapour-cloud reignition; in alcohols (methanol/ethanol), absorption of the water produced in the flame causes abrupt extinction
entries.modificaciones_necesarias: 1) Integrate low-temperature kinetic sub-mechanisms (NTC / RO2 alkyl peroxides) into space propulsion and safety CFD models to predict cool flames (550-750 K); 2) Install UV (OH* at 310 nm) + UV/visible (HCHO* at 395 nm) and IR optical diagnostics in combustion chambers and habitats; 3) Raise the CO2/N2 dilution margin by at least +4% to suppress both the hot-flame and cool-flame branches in heavy hydrocarbons.
entries.fuente: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Repository - Investigation PSI-68
